title: Understanding the immune response to West Nile and Usutu Viruses
official: Virological characterization and analysis of the immune response in subjects with West Nile virus and Usutu virus infection
summary:
Background and study aims
West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) are members of the Orthoflavivirus genus, primarily transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. These pathogens circulate among avian hosts but can occasionally infect mammals, including humans. WNV has been present in Europe since the 1950s and has achieved global distribution, while USUV was first identified in Europe in 1996. Both viruses can cause neuroinvasive disease, with WNV posing a particularly significant threat to elderly and immunocompromised individuals. USUV rarely causes such severe outcomes. Since 2008, WNV has become endemic in several European regions, with a notable increase in epidemic occurrences. Although most human infections with WNV and USUV are asymptomatic, symptomatic cases can range from influenza-like illness to severe neurological complications. Diagnosis relies on serological and molecular tests, but can be challenging due to cross-reactivity among orthoflaviviruses.

The immune response, both innate and adaptive, plays a crucial role in controlling these viral infections. Neutralizing antibodies are essential for defense, as demonstrated in murine models. CD8+ T lymphocytes are key in controlling infection but may also contribute to central nervous system damage. CD4+ T lymphocytes stimulate specific antibody production, support CD8+ T cell function, and directly attack infected cells. The immune response to USUV is less well-studied and requires further investigation. Given the increasing prevalence and potential health impacts of these viruses, continued research into their pathogenesis, immune responses, and potential therapeutic interventions is warranted. This study aims to characterize the immune response induced by West Nile Virus (WNV), Usutu Virus (USUV), and other Orthoflavivirus infections. The goal is to obtain knowledge useful for developing new vaccines against these viruses. It is part of the YELLOW4FLAVI research project funded by the European Commission.

Who can participate?
Healthy male or female adults aged 18-60 years, tested positive for WNV or USUV infection through blood donor screening, without other acute infections or active chronic diseases, willing to provide informed consent, and available for at least two study visits.

What does the study involve?
This is an in vitro study on biological fluids (blood and urine samples) collected from blood donors who tested positive for WNV or USUV during follow-up visits scheduled at 1, 7, 21, 40 days, and 6 and 12 months after the positive donation. No additional blood draws or visits are required beyond those already scheduled for the follow-up of donors who tested positive for West Nile virus. The study will analyze the innate and adaptive immune responses, including antibody levels, T-cell responses, viral replication dynamics, and host genetic factors.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Study participants will benefit from close monitoring for any symptoms that may arise due to WNV or USUV infection, and will receive appropriate support and advice. Additionally, study participants can receive free results of tests on antibody titers induced by the infection, the presence of the virus in blood and urine, and any previous infections by related viruses. By participating, study subjects will also contribute to improving the understanding of immune response mechanisms induced by WNV, USUV, and similar viruses, thus aiding research for vaccine development against these viruses.

A potential risk related to study participation involves blood draws, which will be performed by qualified personnel at the Transfusion Medicine Unit clinics. Although simple, this procedure may cause some discomfort, such as pain or swelling at the needle insertion site. However, no special protective measures are necessary beyond those normally adopted for blood sampling. It is important to note that medical and nursing staff will follow all standard procedures to ensure safety and comfort during this phase of the study. In any case, no additional blood draws will be performed beyond those already scheduled for monitoring subjects who tested positive for WNV NAT.

Where is the study run from?  
UOC di Medicina Trasfusionale (DIMT) Padova - Azienda ULSS6 Euganea, Italy

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
January 2024 to December 2028

Who is funding the study? 
HORIZON EUROPE Framework Programme, European Union.

Who is the main contact? 
Prof Luisa Barzon, luisa.barzon@unipd.it

interventions.name: This is an in vitro study on biological fluids to investigate the adaptive humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in blood donors with West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) infections. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female individuals aged between 18 and 60 years
2. WNV/USUV infection detected through WNV NAT testing as part of blood donor screening
3. Individuals without other acute infections or active chronic diseases, apart from WNV or USUV infection
4. Willingness to provide written informed consent after being adequately informed about the risks and benefits of the study
5. Availability to participate in at least two scheduled study visits
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any individual who, in the investigator's opinion, does not comply with the study objectives and protocol
2. Anticipated absence from the study center during the study period, for example, due to a planned vacation
